html:
Vilnius University was founded in 1579 by the Jesuits, with the charter of King Stephen Báthory of Poland-Lithuania. It is the oldest university in the Baltic states.

It was a spearhead of the Catholic Counter-Reformation in a grand duchy where Protestants and Orthodox were strong. It taught in Latin and later Polish and was among the great universities of eastern Europe.

The Russian tsar closed it in 1832 after the November Uprising against Russian rule. The poet Adam Mickiewicz studied there. Reopened under Polish rule after 1919 and as a Lithuanian university after 1940, it is the leading university of Lithuania today. Compare the University of Tartu in Estonia.
sum: Vilnius University was founded in 1579 by the Jesuits, with the charter of King Stephen Báthory of Poland-Lithuania. It is the oldest university in the Baltic states.
